name: CleanShot X
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Capture screenshots or screen video, annotate them, and copy or save locally

pricing.notes: Primary purchase is a one-time Mac license; optional cloud plans are separate.

tiers.name: App + Cloud Basic
tiers.limits: CleanShot X app; 1 year of updates; 1 GB cloud storage
tiers.notes: One-time purchase: $29; optional update/cloud renewal is $19/year.

tiers.name: App + Cloud Pro
tiers.limits: Latest app updates; unlimited cloud storage; custom domain, branding, security and team features

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier and no direct CleanShot trial; Setapp offers a separate 7-day trial
pricing.billingTerms: one-time Basic license plus optional $19/year renewal, or monthly/annual Pro subscription
pricing.hiddenCosts: The $29 purchase includes updates for only one year and just 1 GB of cloud; continued updates/cloud service costs $19/year, while Pro is per user and subject to fair-use limits.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For CleanShot X, capture screenshots or screen video, annotate them, and copy or save locally. The hard boundary is deep macos integration, scrolling capture, cloud sharing, and years of polish, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Capture screenshots or screen video with microphone audio, trim the result, annotate key moments, copy or save locally, and export a shareable local video.
whatYouLose: deep macOS integration, scrolling capture, cloud sharing, and years of polish
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for CleanShot X because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the One-time license plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for CleanShot X in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture screenshots or screen video with microphone audio, trim the result, annotate key moments, copy or save locally, and export a shareable local video.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
